It may not be retained under any circumstances and must be released immediately; there is no open harvest season, no legal size, and a zero bag/possession limit. If caught, anglers must release it without removing it from the water, per TPWD guidance for prohibited sharks.
No closed season and no maximum size for sheepshead in Texas state waters. Possession limit is double the daily bag limit unless otherwise noted.

rows.season: Year-round (catch and release only - species is prohibited from retention)
rows.notes: Shortfin mako shark is a prohibited species in Texas state waters. It must be released immediately and may not be retained, possessed, or landed by recreational or commercial anglers. This aligns with the 2022 NOAA HMS federal rule prohibiting shortfin mako retention in Atlantic HMS fisheries; TPWD added it to the state prohibited shark list effective Sept 1, 2023.

rows.season: Closed year-round (prohibited species - no retention allowed)
rows.notes: Silky shark is a federally prohibited Atlantic HMS species (must be released immediately with minimal injury) and is also explicitly listed on TPWD's state Prohibited Shark Species list, mirroring the federal rule for consistency across state and federal waters. No size or bag limit applies because retention is never legal.

rows.season: Year-round open water, but retention prohibited (catch-and-release only)
rows.notes: Sixgill shark is on TPWD's prohibited shark species list for Texas state waters. It has a zero bag limit and must be released immediately without removing it from the water. Non-offset, non-stainless steel circle hooks are required when shark fishing in TX state waters.

rows.season: No open season — harvest prohibited year-round
rows.notes: Smalltooth sawfish (and all sawfish species) are federally listed as endangered under the U.S. Endangered Species Act. TPWD confirms it is illegal to target, take, kill, or disturb any sawfish in Texas waters. If unintentionally caught, anglers must use safe release guidelines and report the encounter to the National Sawfish Encounter Database.

Applies to smooth, great, and scalloped hammerhead sharks combined under one 99-inch minimum length rule. The 1-fish daily bag is a combined limit across all allowable shark species (not species-specific). Possession limit is double the daily bag (2). Non-offset, non-stainless steel circle hooks required when fishing for sharks in TX state waters; only the head may be removed at sea, carcass must remain intact.

rows.season: Open year-round except closed November 1 - December 14 (bag limit = 0); valid Sep 1, 2026 - Aug 31, 2027
rows.notes: Applies to all flounder species, hybrids and subspecies (southern, Gulf, etc.) combined. Daily bag is 5 fish with a 15-inch minimum total length and no maximum, EXCEPT during the annual Nov 1 - Dec 14 closure when the bag limit drops to 0 and no flounder may be kept by any method. Possession limit equals the daily bag (5). As of today (Oct 22, 2026), the fishery is currently OPEN (closure begins Nov 1, 2026).
No closed season for Spanish Mackerel in Texas state waters. Possession limit is twice the daily bag limit (30 fish) unless fishing trip lasts longer than one day.

Spiny dogfish (Squalus acanthias) is not on TPWD's prohibited shark species list, so it is regulated as an 'other allowable shark species' with a 64-inch total length minimum and a combined 1-fish daily bag limit shared across all allowable shark species (including Atlantic sharpnose, blacktip, bonnethead). Non-offset, non-stainless steel circle hooks are required when fishing for sharks in TX state waters. Note: spiny dogfish rarely reach 64 inches (adults typically run under 4 ft), so this size limit makes legal harvest practically unlikely — effectively catch-and-release in practice.

Statewide slot limit of 15-20 inches with a 3-fish daily bag (possession limit is double the daily bag, i.e. 6). Additionally, during a license year one spotted seatrout over 28 inches may be retained with a properly completed Spotted Seatrout Tag, and one more over 28 inches with a Bonus Spotted Seatrout Tag — these tagged fish count in ADDITION to the daily bag/possession limit, not as part of it. These statewide limits took effect Sept 1, 2024 and were reaffirmed (moved from §57.985 into §57.981) in a 2025 rulemaking with no change to the actual bag/size numbers.

Striped Bass, its hybrids and subspecies: statewide saltwater bag/length rule, open year-round with no closed season. Possession limit is double the daily bag (10) unless otherwise noted. Applies to Texas state and federal waters as adopted by TPWD (out to 9 nm in Gulf, and 9-200 nm EEZ fish landed in TX).

TPWD regulates all Centropomus species caught in Texas state waters under a single generic 'Snook' category (no species-specific distinction for Swordspine vs. Common Snook). Slot limit is 24-28 inches total length; fish outside this slot must be released. Possession limit is double the daily bag limit (2 fish) per statewide rule. No closed season is listed for snook (unlike flounder, which has a Nov 1-Dec 14 closure), so harvest is open year-round within the slot/bag limit.

Texas state-waters tarpon regulation is a minimum length rule (no maximum/slot) with no closed season. Possession limit is 2 fish (double the daily bag) per statewide rule, but this is a possession limit, not a per-vessel boat limit, so boatLimit is left null. Most anglers practice catch-and-release given the 85-inch minimum.

Tiger shark falls under TPWD's 'Other allowable shark species' category, minimum 64 inches total length, no maximum. Daily bag limit is 1 shark per person per day (in any allowable combination across all legal shark species), with possession limit double the daily bag (2). Non-offset, non-stainless steel circle hooks are required when fishing for sharks in Texas state waters. Only the head may be removed from any retained shark; the carcass must remain intact.

Texas has no closed season for tripletail; the current statewide daily bag limit is 3 fish per angler with a 17-inch minimum total length and no maximum size. Possession limit is generally twice the daily bag per TPWD's standard rule unless otherwise noted.

TPWD's Saltwater Bag and Length Limits table lists White Marlin with No Limit on daily bag or possession, but a stricter Texas state-water minimum size of 86 inches (compared to the federal HMS 66-inch lower-jaw-fork-length minimum). No closed season is listed for this species in Texas state waters. Anglers should note that in federal waters (9-200 nm) NOAA's Atlantic HMS rules also apply, including a combined blue marlin/white marlin/roundscale spearfish per-vessel-per-trip retention limit and a 250-fish annual landings cap for those species combined, plus mandatory 24-hour NOAA landing reports (800-894-5528 or hmspermits.noaa.gov) and a valid HMS Angling/Charterboat permit for federal-water harvest.

Yellowfin tuna is a NOAA Atlantic HMS-managed species; Texas does not set separate state-water limits and follows the federal recreational rule. A valid HMS Angling or Charter/Headboat permit is required to target/retain yellowfin.
